prompt.adult: According to Romans 3:23, who has sinned and fallen short of the glory of God?
prompt.child: Romans 3:23 talks about people who have sinned and fall short of God's glory. Who does it say has sinned?
prompt.teen: Romans 3:23 says some people have sinned and fall short of God's glory. Who?
prompt.older: In Romans 3:23, who is said to have sinned and fallen short of the glory of God?

verses.text: for all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God,

explanation.adult: Romans 3:23 opens by saying who has sinned. Read the first words.
explanation.child: Read Romans 3:23. The very first words tell who has sinned.
explanation.teen: Check Romans 3:23. The first words answer the question.
explanation.older: Romans 3:23 states in its first words who has sinned.

teaching.extended_explanation: Romans 3:22 says there is no difference between people. Romans 3:23 explains why, starting with who has sinned.
teaching.takeaway: All have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.

review.notes: Sprout stage. NKJV excerpt copied from _sprout_nkjv.json (BibleGateway NKJV). Answer is in the cited verse. Manager B/C review: answer “All people” to match the other “who” choices; trimmed padded wrongs.

prompt.adult: Romans 3:24 says people are justified freely by His what?
prompt.child: Romans 3:24 says God makes people right with Him freely. By His what?
prompt.teen: Romans 3:24 says we are made right with God freely. By His what?
prompt.older: According to Romans 3:24, believers are justified freely by His what?

verses.text: being justified freely by His grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus,

explanation.adult: Romans 3:24 tells how people are justified freely. Read the words after "freely by His."
explanation.child: Read Romans 3:24. Find the words "freely by His." The answer comes next.
explanation.teen: Check Romans 3:24. The word you need comes right after "freely by His."
explanation.older: Romans 3:24 supplies the word directly after "freely by His."

teaching.extended_explanation: "Justified" means made right with God. Romans 3:24 says this comes freely, as a gift, and tells what it comes by.
teaching.takeaway: We are justified freely by His grace.

prompt.adult: Romans 5:6 says that at the right time Christ died for whom?
prompt.child: Romans 5:6 says Christ died at just the right time. Who did He die for?
prompt.teen: Romans 5:6 says Christ died at the right time. For whom did He die?
prompt.older: According to Romans 5:6, for whom did Christ die in due time?

verses.text: For when we were still without strength, in due time Christ died for the ungodly.

explanation.adult: Romans 5:6 ends by saying who Christ died for. Read the last words.
explanation.child: Read Romans 5:6. The last words tell who Christ died for.
explanation.teen: Check Romans 5:6. The end of the verse gives the answer.
explanation.older: Romans 5:6 names, in its final words, those for whom Christ died.

teaching.extended_explanation: Romans 5:6 says we were still without strength and could not save ourselves. The end of the verse tells who Christ died for.

review.notes: Sprout stage. NKJV excerpt copied from _sprout_nkjv.json (BibleGateway NKJV). Answer is in the cited verse.

prompt.adult: Christ died for us while we were still sinners. What does Romans 5:8 say God shows us by this?
prompt.child: Christ died for us even while we were still sinners. What does Romans 5:8 say God shows us by that?
prompt.teen: Romans 5:8 says Christ died for us while we were still sinners. What does that show about God?
prompt.older: According to Romans 5:8, what does God demonstrate toward us in that Christ died for us while we were still sinners?

verses.text: But God demonstrates His own love toward us, in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.

explanation.adult: Romans 5:8 begins by saying what God demonstrates toward us. Read the first part of the verse.
explanation.child: Read Romans 5:8. The first part tells what God shows us.
explanation.teen: Check Romans 5:8. The start says what God demonstrates toward us.
explanation.older: Romans 5:8 opens with what God demonstrates toward us.

teaching.extended_explanation: Christ did not wait for people to become good first. Romans 5:8 says what God shows us through that.
teaching.takeaway: God shows His love for us in that Christ died for us while we were still sinners.

review.notes: Sprout stage. NKJV excerpt copied from _sprout_nkjv.json (BibleGateway NKJV). Answer is in the cited verse. Manager B/C review: trimmed a padded wrong so “His own love” is one of two longest corrects.

prompt.adult: Romans 6:23 says the gift of God is what, in Christ Jesus our Lord?
prompt.child: Romans 6:23 talks about a gift from God. What is the gift?
prompt.teen: Romans 6:23 says God gives a gift in Christ Jesus. What is it?
prompt.older: According to Romans 6:23, what is the gift of God in Christ Jesus our Lord?

verses.text: For the wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.

explanation.adult: Romans 6:23 compares two things. Read the second half of the verse.
explanation.child: Read Romans 6:23. The second half tells about God's gift.
explanation.teen: Check Romans 6:23. The answer is in the second half.
explanation.older: Romans 6:23 contrasts wages and a gift; the gift is named in the second half.

teaching.extended_explanation: Romans 6:23 compares what sin pays with what God gives. The gift comes in Christ Jesus our Lord.
teaching.takeaway: The gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.

review.notes: Sprout stage. NKJV excerpt copied from _sprout_nkjv.json (BibleGateway NKJV). Answer is in the cited verse. Manager B/C review: trimmed padded wrongs so “Eternal life” is one of two longest corrects.

prompt.adult: Romans 10:10 talks about believing and confessing. With what does a person believe?
prompt.child: This verse says we believe with one part of us and speak with another. What do we believe with?
prompt.teen: Romans 10:10 links believing and confessing to two different parts of a person. Which part does the believing?
prompt.older: According to Romans 10:10, which speaks of believing unto righteousness and confessing unto salvation, with what does one believe?

verses.text: For with the heart one believes unto righteousness, and with the mouth confession is made unto salvation.

explanation.adult: Romans 10:10 tells what a person believes with. Read the first part of the verse.
explanation.child: This verse says a person believes with something. Read the first words of Romans 10:10.
explanation.teen: Romans 10:10 names what someone believes with. Look at the opening clause.
explanation.older: Read the first half of Romans 10:10 for what one believes with.

teaching.extended_explanation: The verse pairs two parts of a person: one for believing and one for confessing. Read the first half to see what a person believes with.
teaching.takeaway: With the heart one believes unto righteousness.

prompt.child: Romans 10:13 makes a promise to whoever calls on the name of the LORD. What will happen to them?

prompt.older: According to Romans 10:13, what shall happen to whoever calls on the name of the LORD?

verses.text: For “whoever calls on the name of the LORD shall be saved.”

explanation.adult: Romans 10:13 ends with the promise. Read the last word of the verse.
explanation.child: Read Romans 10:13. The last word tells what will happen.
explanation.teen: Check Romans 10:13. The promise is the last word.
explanation.older: Romans 10:13 concludes with the promise in its final word.

prompt.adult: According to Romans 10:17, what does faith come by?
prompt.child: Romans 10:17 tells how faith comes to people. What does it come by?
prompt.teen: Romans 10:17 explains how faith comes. What does it come by?
prompt.older: According to Romans 10:17, by what does faith come?

verses.text: So then faith comes by hearing, and hearing by the word of God.

explanation.adult: Romans 10:17 links faith with the word of God. Read the first part of the verse.
explanation.child: Read Romans 10:17. The first part tells what faith comes by.
explanation.teen: Check Romans 10:17. The first part answers the question.
explanation.older: Romans 10:17 states the source of faith in its opening clause.

teaching.extended_explanation: Romans 10:14-17 asks how people can believe if no one tells them. Verse 17 sums it up and connects it to the word of God.
teaching.takeaway: Faith comes by hearing, and hearing by the word of God.
